Subject: Post-demo: Kooplia integration checklist, SDK auth, and prompt governance roadmap

Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today — great conversation. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we have a single place to iterate: 

What we demoed
- Redwood hosted inference + Dedicated options for predictable throughput
- SDK quickstart (node/python) and auth options
- Structured output / tool-calling for your domain-specific actions
- Embeddings + optional reranker flow for semantic search
- Prompt templates and a governance model (versioning + red-team)

Open items for Kooplia (please confirm):
1) Primary infra: you mentioned GCP/Kubernetes — can you confirm cluster/private networking constraints and whether a proxy/NAT sits in front?
2) Auth: do you want short-lived tokens via OAuth or long-lived API keys with rotation? Any KMS/HSM requirements?
3) Throughput expectations: what steady-state and peak qps should we plan for?
4) Embeddings: where do you prefer embeddings stored (your DB, managed vector store, or Redwood-managed)? Any PII considerations?
5) Prompt governance: who owns system prompts and red-team reviews on your side?

Our proposed next steps
- I’ll loop in engineering + security to confirm SDK auth patterns and a recommended routing/burst policy. (E2: Rishi to lead routing/embeddings; Karthik to validate SDK integration)
- Draft a short integration checklist and a prompt-versioning proposal for review (attached)
- Set up a 60-min POC run in a sandbox with sample dataset — propose the week of 10/25

Attachments: kooplia-mvp-integration-checklist.xlsx (first pass), prompt-versioning-proposal.md

Can you reply with answers for items 1–4 and an initial contact for legal/contract review?

Best,
Jasmine Liu

Thanks Jasmine — great demo. Quick answers inline below: 

1) Primary infra: yes, GKE on GCP. We run in a single VPC with private clusters; egress is NATed through an egress gateway.
2) Auth: prefer API keys with automated rotation. We have an HSM-backed KMS for master key storage.
3) Throughput: baseline ~40 req/s, peak bursts to 200 req/s (short spikes). Latency SLO target 200ms per request for small models, 500–800ms for larger generations.
4) Embeddings: prefer we host vectors in our managed Postgres + PGVector initially; open to Redwood-managed vector store later. PII: customer names and emails are PII and must be redacted from embeddings.

Prompt ownership: Priya will own the product prompts; I’ll coordinate with our security/infra for red-team reviews. Legal is CC’d (contracts@kooplia.ai) for the SLA & data controls.

We’d like a short SDK pairing session (30–45m) to get auth set up and try the structured output support. Week of 10/25 works for us.

Sam

Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo — security & prompt governance checklist

Adding the security checklist items we’ll need to sign off on before a POC goes live.

Security ask-list (initial):
- KMS/HSM: confirm AES-256 keys in HSM for master key; provide key rotation policy. We can support both Redwood-managed KMS and customer-managed KMS via gcp-kms.
- Auth: API keys are fine but we need rotation + short TTL on issued child keys. mTLS can be supported for Dedicated customers; please confirm whether Kooplia wants mTLS for service-to-service in POC.
- Embeddings/PII: require opt-in redaction step before embeddings are written. Show us data flows: where vectors are stored, retention policy, and delete-on-request mechanics.
- Audit & logs: need request-level tracing (token-level cost, model used) and immutable audit logs for the POC period.
- Prompt injection mitigations: system-prompt locking (server-side), user input sanitization, explicit turn-limits, and an allowlist/denylist for tool-calls. We also recommend a red-team plan: automated fuzzing + human review cycle before production. See attached prompt-versioning-proposal.md for a proposed workflow (authoring -> version tag -> test-suite -> rollout).

Deliverables I need from engineering
- Short architecture diagram showing SDK <-> egress gateway <-> Redwood endpoints + where KMS sits
- Suggested API-key rotation schedule and how we’ll enforce TTL
- A minimal red-team test plan (fuzz inputs + sample injected prompts)

I’ll coordinate sign-off with Legal once those items are in place.

-neha
Neha Kapoor
